cards.text: Stephen, one of the seven men chosen to help with the church's daily food distribution (Acts 6:1-5), is standing in front of the Sanhedrin, the Jewish ruling council (Acts 6:12). False witnesses say he never stops speaking against this holy place and against the law, and I bet you could hear a crumb drop in that room (Acts 6:13). Then the high priest turns to Stephen.

cards.question: Stephen stands before the council with false witnesses speaking against him. What does the high priest ask him?

answers.text: Who gave him the right to teach

cards.text: Stephen doesn't give a yes or a no. He says, “Brothers and fathers, listen to me!” and goes ALL the way back, like when you ask somebody how their day was and they start with the year they were born.

cards.question: Stephen starts with the God of glory appearing to the man he calls “our father,” back when he was still in Mesopotamia. Who is it?

cards.text: God tells him, ‘Leave your country and your kindred and go to the land I will show you.’ No name, no map, and Abraham GOES: first to Haran, then, after his father dies, into the land the council is living in now.

cards.question: Abraham doesn't own one foot of that land. But God promises to give it to Abraham and his ___, even though he has no ___ yet.

cards.text: God also tells him his descendants will be foreigners in a strange land, enslaved and mistreated four hundred years. Four HUNDRED, and I thought a few years in a junk drawer was rough.

cards.question: God says He will punish the nation that enslaves Abraham's descendants. Afterward, where does He say they will worship Him?

answers.text: In the land He brought Abraham to
In the land where they were slaves
In the land Abraham left behind

cards.question: God gives Abraham the covenant of circumcision, and his line runs through Isaac and Jacob to Jacob's twelve sons, the patriarchs. Why do they sell their brother Joseph as a slave into Egypt?

answers.text: Because they were jealous of him
Because their father told them to

cards.question: But God is with Joseph and rescues him from all his troubles. He gives Joseph favor and wisdom in front of Pharaoh king of Egypt. What does Pharaoh make Joseph?

answers.text: Ruler over Egypt and his household

cards.text: Then famine hits Egypt and Canaan, and Jacob sends his sons to Egypt for grain. On their second visit, Joseph reveals who he is and sends for his father and all his relatives, seventy-five in all.

cards.question: Jacob and his sons die in Egypt, and their people grow greatly in number. Then a new king rises who knew nothing of Joseph, and he treats Israel's people kindly.

cards.text: He oppresses them and forces them to abandon their infants so they would die. At that time Moses is born, and when he's set outside, Pharaoh's daughter brings him up as her own son.

cards.question: Moses grows up educated in all the wisdom of the Egyptians. At forty, he strikes down an Egyptian who is mistreating one of his people, and he assumes they'll understand that God is using him to ___ them.

His people don't understand. The next day Moses tries to make peace between two Israelites, and one pushes him aside: “Who made you ruler and judge over us? Do you want to kill me as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?” Where does Moses flee to live as a foreigner?

cards.text: Forty years later, an angel appears to Moses in the flames of a burning bush near Mount Sinai, and the voice of the Lord comes to him. The Lord has seen His people's oppression in Egypt, and He's sending Moses back, like the job you ran out on calling forty years later to say start MONDAY.

cards.question: The man who pushed Moses aside asked, “Who made you ruler and judge?” Stephen says God sent that same Moses to be their ruler and ___.

Moses leads them out with wonders and signs in Egypt, at the Red Sea and for forty years in the wilderness. Stephen says Moses told them God would raise up a prophet for them from among their brothers. A prophet like whom?
Stephen says Moses received living words to pass on to them. But their fathers refused to ___ him.

cards.text: In their hearts they turn back to Egypt and tell Aaron, Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), ‘Make us gods who will go before us!’ They make a calf and rejoice in the works of their hands, and God turns away from them.

cards.question: Stephen quotes the book of the prophets about the tabernacle of Molech and the star of Rephan, idols they made to worship. Where does God say He will send them?

answers.text: Out to the desert of Midian

cards.text: Pause right there, friend. Stephen's still got the floor, and he is NOT finished.

findings.problem: Six of the twelve choice cards in this stop (cards 2, 7, 10, 13, 16 and 19) require recall or luck rather than reasoning from the earlier cards: there is no usable clue for Abraham's identity, the brothers' motive, the new king's behavior, Midian, the prophet being like Moses, or Babylon. That is more than a few discovery questions in one stop and leaves no more than half of its choices as informed guesses.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
